title: Graded Degradation: Customer SLA Scorer and Operator Playbook
author: Laila Brooks
body:
Summary:
This document defines the Graded Degradation framework: a deterministic, observable scoring system that prioritizes tenants/customers during capacity scarcity and drives operator actions and automated mitigations. It pairs a numerical Customer SLA Score with a stepwise degradation playbook and dashboard contract so operators and automation make consistent, auditable trade-offs to preserve high-value SLAs.

Scope:
- Applies to all multi-tenant inference routing (router, allocator-service, model-proxy) and runtime subsystems that perform shedding, prefetch throttling, and model-variant fallback.
- Not for billing/time-based quota enforcement or legal compliance evictions (see billing ops playbook).

Owner & Contacts:
- Owner: Platform Operations (operator-oncall@redwood.ai)
- Primary author: Laila Brooks (Platform SRE)
- Reviewers: Marco Alvarez (Runtime), Chen Li (Product), Riley Thompson (Customer Success)

When to use:
1) Real-time capacity pressure identified (SLO burn >= 10% sustained for 5 minutes).
2) Cross-region model shortage with spillover risk.
3) Sudden token surge that threatens P99 latency for SLA-tier customers.

Customer SLA Score (overview):
- Composite numerical score 0..100; higher means higher SLA priority.
- Components: SLA_Tier (weight 40%), Error_Impact (weight 25%), Latency_Exposure (weight 20%), Recent_SLA_Burn (weight 15%).
- FinalScore = round(0.4*SLA_TierScore + 0.25*ErrorImpactScore + 0.2*LatencyExposureScore + 0.15*RecentBurnScore)

Scoring details (component mapping):
- SLA_TierScore: production-enterprise=100, production-standard=60, trial=20, internal=10.
- ErrorImpactScore: based on percent of requests returning 5xx in last 5m normalized to 100 (e.g., 3% 5xx -> 30).
- LatencyExposureScore: normalized P99 latency percentile mapped to 0..100 (below target -> low score).
- RecentBurnScore: SLO burn window 5m–1h, normalized mapping with hysteresis to avoid flapping.

Example scoring pseudocode:
1) Collect metrics: p99_latency_ms, error_rate_5xx_pct, slo_burn_pct, customer_tier
2) map SLA_TierScore = lookup(customer_tier)
3) ErrorImpactScore = min(100, error_rate_5xx_pct * 10)
4) LatencyExposureScore = clamp(100 - ((p99_latency_ms - target_ms)/target_ms * 100), 0, 100)
5) RecentBurnScore = clamp(slo_burn_pct * 2, 0, 100)
6) FinalScore = round(0.4*SLA_TierScore + 0.25*ErrorImpactScore + 0.2*LatencyExposureScore + 0.15*RecentBurnScore)

Degradation Bands (operator-visible):
- Band A (Score 85–100): No degradation. Highest priority routing, warmset cache reservation, prefetch affinity = true, model-variant fallback to same-quality quantized variants only.
- Band B (Score 60–84): Soft degradation. Allow model-variant fallback to lower-cost quantized variant, reduce batch window max by 10–20%, deprioritize prefetch, limit long-context requests (>2048 tokens).
- Band C (Score 30–59): Aggressive soft degradation. Increase batching aggressiveness for non-SLA traffic, enable token caps per-request (e.g., 512), route noncritical + bulk jobs to DedicatedSpot pools or cold-path.
- Band D (Score 0–29): Preemption / hard degrade. Disable nonessential features (reranking, heavy tool-calls), queue or reject (429) best-effort customers, surface emergency notice to customer-facing teams.

Operator Runbook (step-by-step):
1) Detection: Confirm platform metric signals: overall SLO burn > 10% (5m sustained) OR allocator-service queue depth > 95th percentile.
2) Compute Scores: Trigger scoring job (k8s job: scorers/customer-sla-scorer) for active tenants; publish scores to telemetry topic `platform.sla_scores`.
3) Review Dashboard: Open Graded Degradation dashboard (see Dashboard and Alerts) and verify top 5 at-risk tenants and their Bands.
4) If any enterprise tenant in Band C or worse: apply emergency throttles on best-effort tenants via `allocatorctl adjust-band --band C --policy soft-throttle`.
5) If multiple enterprise tenants in Band D or global P99 exceeds 3x target: escalate to SEV process (see Incident Process) and begin manual capacity buys / region failover.
6) Post-Action: Annotate the incident in `#platform-operators` channel with score snapshots and applied policies.

Dashboard and Alerts (contract):
- Dashboard MUST show: per-tenant FinalScore, Band, trend over 1h/6h/24h, p50/p95/p99 latencies, 5xx rate, queue depth, current routed variant.
- Alert rules (examples):
  - sla-scorer-high-burn: fire when >= 3 enterprise tenants score <= 50 for 10m. (Severity: P2)
  - band-d-enterprise-imminent: fire when any enterprise tenant transitions to Band D (Immediate page to oncall + slack pings). (Severity: P1)
  - scoring-pipeline-failure: when the scoring job misses 2 consecutive runs. (Severity: P2)
- Visualization: small multiples for top-20 tenants; color by Band with timestamped annotation for operator actions.

Automated Actions (safe defaults):
- Automation is allowed only when scoring job is healthy and operator approval is present (two-step):
  - Step 1: Auto-apply Band B policies for tenants with score in 60–74 for > 5m.
  - Step 2: Auto-notify operators and require manual confirm to escalate to Band C/D automated actions.
- All automated actions must write to audit-log `platform.audit.shed_actions` and include `reason`, `score_snapshot`, `operator_override` fields.

CLI examples and operator tools:
- Run scorer locally: `kubectl -n platform exec -it $(kubectl -n platform get pod -l app=scorer -o name) -- python scorer/run.py --window 5m --emit`
- Force re-evaluate customer: `allocatorctl force-evaluate --tenant-id tenant-123 --reason "manual check"`
- Apply soft-throttle policy: `allocatorctl adjust-band --band C --policy soft-throttle --dry-run`

Rollback & Recovery guidance:
- If degradation causes customer-visible regression (reported by CS): rollback in reverse order of application. Steps:
  1) Revert model-variant fallback for affected tenant: `allocatorctl set-variant --tenant tenant-123 --variant pinned`
  2) Undo token caps: `allocatorctl set-tenant-limits --tenant tenant-123 --max-tokens 4096`
  3) Restore prefetch affinity and warmset reservations.
- If rollback fails, escalate to Runtime oncall and open SEV with `severity: customer-impact` and include scoring snapshot.

Post-incident actions and metrics to record:
- For each incident record: start/end time, top-5 tenant scores, list of policies applied, time-to-first-action, customer-impacted request count, estimated cost delta.
- Add a 2-week perf-runbook item: simulate same workload with synthetic tenants, validate score stability and operator runbook adequacy.

Appendix: Metrics and thresholds (recommended defaults)
- Platform SLO targets (example):
  - Realtime API (enterprise): P99 tail latency <= 250ms, error rate <0.5%
  - Realtime API (standard): P99 <= 500ms, error rate <1%
- Scorer cadence: every 60s with 5m sliding window; fallback to 5m cron if pipeline cold-start.
- Queue depth thresholds: allocator queue > 80% => pre-warning; >95% => immediate attention.

Operational notes / caveats:
- Hysteresis: scores must have 2-window persistence to avoid oscillation (i.e., band change only if score crosses threshold in 2 consecutive runs).
- Telemetry cost: disable full per-request tracing while in Band C/D for best-effort tenants to conserve sampling budget.
- Customer-facing comms: CS must be notified proactively for any enterprise tenant when Band B -> C transition occurs.

Related runbooks and pages:
- See tenant-safety-scorecard-and-auto-mitigation-patterns (systems-and-services) for scoring refinements.
- See emergency-model-swap-and-token-surge-mitigation (runbooks) for model fallback templates and playbook snippets.
